article.title: AIPAC Get What It Paid For
article.author: William J. Astore
article.content: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. I made the mistake of going on X/Twitter this morning, where I came across Hakeem Jeffries saying he and the Democrats are going to address the affordability crisis in America. Is he going to do that by raising the federal minimum wage to $20 an hour? Of course not. He provided no specifics. Here’s an excerpt from a recent interview of Jeffries: So from our standpoint, we want to do things like end this reckless and costly war of choice in Iran, which has made life way too expensive. We need to stop the Trump Tariffs. We need to reverse the Medicaid cuts that put the health insurance of millions of Americans at risk and threatens to close hospitals all over the place. We certainly need to reverse the SNAP cuts. And we need to extend the Affordable Care Act tax credits. OK, so he wants to end the Iran war, but he doesn’t say how. I’ve seen where he’s against cutting Congressional funding for that war, which would be the quickest way to end it. He’s against impeaching President Trump for starting “this reckless and costly war of choice in Iran.” So what, exactly, is Jeffries going to do except bloviate? Furthermore, we know he’s on the AIPAC payroll big time, and Zionist Israel wants this war, so chances are Jeffries will do nothing more than blather on. Related: Is the Media Selling Another War? The Iran Dirty Bomb Allegations There’s no vision, no action, coming from Jeffries. At best, he wants to return to the Biden years, tinkering around the edges, supporting policies that are attractive to health insurance companies, big pharma, the status quo. Is that what the “Blunami” was all about? Incremental change to return us (if we’re lucky) to 2022? Jeffries opposes Medicare for All or any other single-payer government health care system. He refuses to support raising the minimum wage to $20 an hour. (He says it should be raised but provides no figure, so maybe he thinks $7.50 might be a decent hourly rate.) He won’t oppose weapons sales to Israel and he’ll never say Israel is engaged in a genocide in Gaza. Nor will he call for major cuts to Pentagon spending. Jeffries is Obama 2.0 without the oratorical skills and charisma. Just as Obama discarded his followers and a progressive agenda after his dramatic victory in 2008—wait a moment, I take that back. Obama was never really for “change” in the way that his followers believed him to be. As Congressman Dennis Kucinich said about Obama, “check his scorecard” in the Senate, where Obama was basically a neoliberal Clintonist. When President Obama bailed out the banks and rewarded the bankers while screwing American workers and homeowners, that was eminently predictable based on his scorecard and the fact that Wall Street had embraced him and funded his campaign. Check Hakeem Jeffries’ scorecard and who funds him and it’s obvious he’s going to betray American workers. And the danger is what these workers reach for in 2028 when they turn away from his empty and exploitative phoniness. They are likely to turn toward a populist Republican promising a form of vengeance through retrograde policies. As I looked at that image of Jeffries, the song “Smiling Faces” popped into my head. Some choice lyrics: Smiling faces, smiling faces, sometimes They don’t tell the truth Smiling faces, smiling faces tell lies and I got proof Oh, oh, yeah Can you blame workers for wanting some form of vengeance, no matter how wrongheaded or counterproductive, when they’ve been betrayed so often by liars like Jeffries? What a great song!
